outcome: Breastfeeding initiation rates (exclusive or partial BF)

Comorbidities (gestational diabetes, pregestational diabetes, chronic hypertension, severe preeclampsia, obstructive sleep apnea, asthma, gestational hypertension, polycystic ovary syndrome, gastroesophageal reflux disease, anemia)
cohort: The study included 1780 women (890 with morbid obesity and 890 with extreme obesity), matched by race, parity, and year of delivery, who delivered singletons at or after 34 weeks gestation between 2013 and 2021, excluding those with bariatric surgery or infants with major malformations.
finding: Women with extreme obesity had a higher prevalence of several comorbidities and lower rates of intention to breastfeed, exclusive breastfeeding, and overall breastfeeding initiation at discharge compared to women with morbid obesity.
mod_finding: Cesarean deliveries were significantly higher in the extreme obesity group (62%) compared to the morbid obesity group (44%).
